judged_text: The `update` action accepts a PUT and returns the serialized embedding but never persists any request parameters, making it a silent no-op endpoint, and the admin-embedding controller's saveChanges action still calls it. Any admin who wires a future editable field into the Embedding UI (the saveChanges action already exists in admin-embedding.js.es6 line 7) gets a success response while their changes are silently discarded.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb) handles a PUT (`put "customize/embedding"`) but only re-renders `@embedding` and does not read or persist any request params. The Ember admin controller `saveChanges()` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6) still calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, so the endpoint exists and returns success without performing an update. This isn’t a user-visible defect right now because no editable embedding fields are shown/sent (hosts are saved via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded completeness/behavior concern: a PUT update route that is effectively a no-op.
